name: Discharge Planner
description: Adult inpatient discharge planning + outpatient medication review. Marketplace-publishable A2A specialist sharing the TrustedRisk MCP backend. Advertises 9 skills: Safe discharge review, Medication safety review, PHI leakage check, Patient-language discharge counseling, Empiric antibiotic + de-escalation, Oncology cycle decision + RECIST response, Multilingual patient-facing rendering, Terminology + comorbidity-index normalization, Discharge order set + adherence + HEDIS gaps + PROM. FHIR context propagated via the A2A v1 FHIR-context extension; tools see the FHIRContext via the shared ContextVar without ever surfacing the bearer token to the LLM prompt. Every recommendation surfaces a calibrated CI when applicable, a deterministic safety gate, an abstain trigger when uncertainty or demographic bias is high, a 4-critic ensemble vote (clinical_safety + fairness + evidence + llm_judge) with bounded plan revision, a fairness audit by demographic subgroup, and a longitudinal patient timeline that surfaces drift across encounters.

_bundles._doc: Thematic groupings for client-side discovery. Tools may appear in multiple bundles (e.g. ground_claim, fairness_audit). The runtime exposes BUNDLES via the tools package (mcp_server.tools.list_bundles()).

skills.name: Safe discharge review
skills.description: Review a patient chart and produce a discharge action recommendation with calibrated risk estimates, evidence grounding, medication-reconciliation safety check, fairness audit by demographic subgroup, PHI check, and explicit abstain if uncertainty is high. Includes a self-critique stage that reviews internal consistency before emitting the final DecisionCard. Uses SHARP-on-MCP for FHIR context propagation.
examples: Can patient Jane Doe (Enc/A123) be discharged home safely?
Review the discharge plan for this patient and flag any concerns.
What is the 30-day readmission risk for this patient and what's the recommended disposition?

skills.name: Medication safety review
skills.description: Stateless medication-reconciliation + polypharmacy + drug-drug-interaction analysis on a structured med list. Does not require a FHIR Patient context. Useful for batch pre-admission med review or for callers that already have an admission/discharge med-list pair.
examples: Review these discharge medications for interactions: warfarin 5 mg, ibuprofen 600 mg, lisinopril 10 mg.
Compare the admission and discharge med lists and flag any safety concerns.

skills.name: PHI leakage check
skills.description: Scan arbitrary clinical text for PHI entities and produce a redaction map. Does not require FHIR patient context.
examples: Scan this discharge summary for PHI.
Does this note contain any protected information?

skills.name: Patient-language discharge counseling
skills.description: Generate a structured, patient-friendly discharge summary from the structured medication list, LACE risk score, and recommended action. Output is targeted at a 6th-grade reading level and contains five sections (Your Medications, Follow-up Appointments, Warning Signs, Daily Activities, Questions to Ask). Templates are deterministic — every statement binds to a structured input, so no medication or dosage can be hallucinated. Optional LLM polish (TRUSTEDRISK_COUNSELING_LLM_POLISH=1) paraphrases prose without changing facts. Reusable for outpatient med-review counseling (set lace_score=0).
examples: Generate a 6th-grade-level discharge summary for this patient's medication list.
Write patient-language warning signs for someone leaving on warfarin and lisinopril.
Produce an outpatient counseling sheet for an 82-year-old on 11 chronic medications.

skills.name: Empiric antibiotic + de-escalation
skills.description: Two stewardship tools: (1) compute_empiric_antibiotic_selection ranks empiric regimens by infection source (urinary / pneumonia / SSTI / etc.) and severity (uncomplicated → septic shock), incorporating LOCAL antibiogram data (e.g. ESBL prevalence > 15% pulls carbapenem to top pick), patient allergies, renal function, and MRSA / Pseudomonas risk; (2) compute_antibiotic_de_escalation takes the current regimen + identified pathogen + susceptibility pattern and recommends the narrowest acceptable agent + IV-to-PO switch when the IDSA "5 Cs" criteria (afebrile 24h, hemodynamically stable, tolerating PO, alert, no malabsorption) are met.
examples: Pick empiric antibiotics for complicated UTI with sepsis, PCN allergy, local ESBL 22%.
De-escalate pip-tazo IV for an E. coli ESBL UTI on day 3.
Decide IV-to-PO switch for a patient afebrile 24h but still NPO.

skills.name: Oncology cycle decision + RECIST response
skills.description: Two oncology tools: (1) compute_chemo_dose_adjustment decides whether the next chemo cycle should proceed (full or reduced dose), be delayed, held, or discontinued — based on hematologic recovery (ANC, platelets), renal function (cisplatin holds, carboplatin Calvert), hepatic function (anthracycline / taxane bilirubin gates), and ECOG performance status; growth-factor recommendation included for high-FN-risk regimens; (2) compute_oncology_treatment_response implements RECIST 1.1 categorical response (CR / PR / SD / PD / NE) from target lesion measurements + new-lesion / non-target progression flags, with a decision implication (continue / dose-escalation / switch / palliative / repeat imaging).
examples: Decide cycle 4 of carboplatin/pemetrexed with ANC 1100, eGFR 58.
Compute RECIST 1.1 for a patient with target lesions shrinking from 62 mm to 41 mm.
Adjust doxorubicin dose for a patient with bilirubin 2.5.

skills.name: Multilingual patient-facing rendering
skills.description: Three patient-facing tools (PATIENT-1/2/3): compute_translate_discharge_counseling (en/es/zh/vi/ar paraphrase-only, structured bullets immutable), compute_patient_faq (anticipated patient questions + answers from the structured DecisionCard), compute_caregiver_summary (caregiver-language summary for hand-off).
examples: Translate the discharge counseling into Vietnamese.
Generate the top 5 FAQs for a patient discharged on warfarin.
Caregiver summary for a 90y patient discharged with delirium watch.

skills.name: Terminology + comorbidity-index normalization
skills.description: Four DATA-1/2/3/4 tools: compute_charlson_elixhauser_index (Quan 2005 + van Walraven 2009), compute_normalize_observations (LOINC), compute_rxnorm_ddi_lookup (NIH RxNav DDI graph), compute_umls_concept_map (UMLS Metathesaurus crosswalk). Used for cross-EHR normalisation upstream of the clinical bundles.
examples: Compute Charlson + Elixhauser for a patient with CHF + DM2 + CKD.
DDI lookup on warfarin + amiodarone + amoxicillin.
UMLS crosswalk SNOMED 44054006 → ICD-10.

skills.name: Discharge order set + adherence + HEDIS gaps + PROM
skills.description: Four LIB-1/2/3/4 tools: compute_order_set (template-driven structured discharge orders), compute_medication_adherence_predictor (driver-list + risk score), compute_care_gap_detector (HEDIS-mapped open gaps), compute_prom_influence (PROMIS-29 / EQ-5D-5L → QALY delta + action-dominance shift hint).
examples: Generate the discharge order set for a high-risk CHF patient.
Predict adherence risk for a 5-medication regimen on Medicare.
Detect open HEDIS care gaps for a Type 2 DM patient.
Compute QALY-30d from a PROMIS-29 score set.

extensions.description: A2A v1 FHIR-context extension. The platform delivers FHIR credentials in `Message.metadata` keyed by this URI, with camelCase fields {fhirUrl, fhirToken, patientId, fhirRefreshToken?, fhirRefreshTokenUrl?}. TrustedRisk consumes the metadata in its before-model hook, populates the shared FHIRContext ContextVar, and never lets the credentials reach the LLM prompt. See https://docs.promptopinion.ai/fhir-context/a2a-fhir-context.html.

selfCritique.description: Every clinical recommendation passes through a 4-critic ensemble (clinical_safety + fairness + evidence + llm_judge) that may downgrade confidence, force abstain, or request a replay before the response is emitted. The LLM critic has a deterministic floor (pass-through approval) so it never blocks unilaterally.

memoryLayer.description: Prior DecisionCards for the same patient are retrieved from a SQLite-backed memory store. When a valid (non-expired, same-model-version) card is found, it can serve directly; otherwise a fresh tool chain runs and detect_recommendation_drift flags any meaningful change vs the prior.

temporalValidity.description: Every RiskEstimate carries a valid_until timestamp scaled by clinical-risk severity (high LACE → 4h, moderate → 12h, low → 24h). Expired cards force a re-call.

fairnessAuditCalibration.description: Subgroup-multiplier baseline is calibrated on the receiving cohort (internal calibration workflow output) and falls back to literature defaults (HRRP/HCUP/JAMA) when the calibrated artifact is absent.

counterfactualExplanation.description: Per-factor what-if sweep shows how each LACE component contributes to the predicted risk and identifies a minimum-modification path that would flip the recommendation tier.

multiTenant.description: Optional OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant (RFC 6749 §4.4) with per-client allowed_fhir_servers allowlist enforces tenant isolation: a token issued for tenant A cannot be used to query tenant B's FHIR endpoint.

auditTrail.description: Append-only HIPAA-style audit log (PHI-redacted SHA-256 hashing) plus an RFC 6962 Merkle audit chain for tamper-evidence; reproducibility archive enables byte-identical replay of any historical decision.

rightToExplanation.description: GDPR Art. 22 / EU AI Act Art. 13 right-to-explanation surface — every DecisionCard is paired with a patient-friendly audit summary on demand.

differentialPrivacyEquity.description: Equity dashboard publishes subgroup intervention / abstain / risk rates with Laplace-mechanism differential privacy.

oauth2SecurityScheme.description: Optional bearer-token authentication (RFC 6749 §4.4). Disabled by default; enable via TRUSTEDRISK_OAUTH_ENABLED=1.

apiKeySecurityScheme.description: Static API-key authentication for marketplace-mediated A2A calls. Configured via TRUSTEDRISK_API_KEYS env var (comma-separated). When set, every A2A call must carry `X-API-Key` matching one of the configured values.
apiKeySecurityScheme.name: X-API-Key
